text.p: Turkish fan, electric stove and household goods producer Raks Elektrikli Ev Aletleri Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. (Raksev) targets $32 million total sales in 1997, a senior company official said on Monday.

"We increased our turnover to 3.45 trillion lira in 1996 from 1.34 trillion lira in 1995 and we aim to raise it by approximately 60 percent to 5.5 trillion lira this year," Oguz Dagli, a board member of the parent company Raks Holding, told Reuters.
Shares of Raksev opened at 45,000 lira on Monday and eased to 44,000 at the close in Istanbul.
The company is planning to set up assembly lines in its major export markets of Romania, Bulgaria, Greece, Macedonia and Serbia to avoid high tariffs on finished goods exports to those countries.
"We will test the north African market for our electric stoves where there are no central-heating systems and we sell fans," Dagli said.
Dagli said they would also export stoves to the Caucasus and central-Asian countries.
The company is planning to increase stove production to 500,000 units and fan production to one million units within two years. It produced 150,000 units stove and 340,000 units fan in 1996.
Raksev generates 55-60 percent of its total turnover from fans and air-conditioners, 30 percent from stoves and the rest from electrical kitchenware.
It reported 3.45 trillion lira total sales in 1996, against 1.34 trillion lira in 1995. Its net profit rose to 164 billion lira in 1996, from 94 billion lira in 1995.
